symbols.name: FullLawClass
symbols.type: class of one-unit full-data causal laws

symbols.name: ObservedLawClass
symbols.type: observed-data image of the causal class

symbols.name: tau
symbols.role: observed-law CATE, causally identified on the observed image

symbols.name: V
symbols.role: squared separation from the constant-CATE null

symbols.name: I
symbols.role: set containing every legal constant CATE

symbols.name: PropensityClass
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{\alpha,L,\epsilon}=\{f\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L):\epsilon\le f(x)\le1-\epsilon\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\)

symbols.name: phiKnown
symbols.role: test whose second input is the exact propensity function

symbols.name: YuLearnerRegime
symbols.def: \(\mathsf Y_n\) denotes \(\|\widehat e_n-e\|_{L^2(P)}=o_P(n^{-1/4})\), \(\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\|\widehat\mu_{a,n}-\mu_a\|_{L^2(P)}=o_P(n^{-1/4})\), \(\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau\|_{L^2(P)}=o_P(n^{-1/4})\), and \(\lvert\widehat{\bar\tau}_n-\bar\tau\rvert=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), the learner-rate part of Yu (2026), Assumption 4

symbols.name: YuRegularity
symbols.def: \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{Yu},n}(P)\) denotes the non-learner conditions in Yu (2026), Assumptions 1--3 and Theorem 1, including Assumption 3(ii)'s boundary-nondegeneracy requirement and the stated fold and moment conditions

symbols.name: cDGSHunt
symbols.type: weighted projection coefficient for the hunted interaction

symbols.name: DGSRegularity
symbols.def: \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{DGS},n}(P)\) denotes Assumptions 1--5 and Theorem 1(a)--(b) of Dhawan, Guo and Shah (2026) for \(\ell_{\mathrm{DGS}},\mathcal F_{\mathrm{DGS}},\mathcal G_{\mathrm{DGS},P}\), including their conditional score-variance lower bound, estimation remainders, direction nondegeneracy, and conditional Lyapunov condition

symbols.name: DGSCondition
symbols.def: \(\mathsf D_n(\kappa_n,\delta_n)\) denotes \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{DGS},n}(P)\), \(V_{\mathrm{DGS}}(P)\ge\delta_n\), \(\inf_P P\{\operatorname{Corr}_P(s_P(U),\xi_P(U)\mid\widehat h_n)>\kappa_n\}\to1\), and \(n\kappa_n^2\delta_n\to\infty\), with the infimum over the DGS-admissible comparison class at energy at least \(\delta_n\)

symbols.name: Rupper
symbols.role: candidate full-class upper rate, not a claimed minimax answer

symbols.name: cRate
symbols.def: \(c_{\mathrm{rate}}>0\), derived by the minimax lower-bound statements

symbols.name: CRate
symbols.def: \(C_{\mathrm{rate}}<\infty\), derived by the uniform upper-bound statements

symbols.name: n0
symbols.def: \(n_0\), derived by the uniform statements as a function only of \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon\)

symbols.name: PiK
symbols.def: the \(L^2(\lambda)\)-projection onto regular-grid tensor polynomials of degree \(\lceil\gamma\rceil\) and rank \(k\), including constants

symbols.name: phiBasis
symbols.def: \(\boldsymbol\varphi_k=(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_k)\) is the fixed orthonormal basis defining \(\Pi_k\)

symbols.name: PEll
symbols.def: the \(L^2(\lambda)\)-projection onto regular-grid tensor polynomials of degree \(\lceil\alpha\vee\beta\rceil\) and rank \(\ell\)

symbols.name: HalfSets
symbols.type: deterministic pair of disjoint index sets
symbols.def: \((\mathcal I_1,\mathcal I_2)\) is the fixed partition of \(\{1,\ldots,2N\}\) with \(\lvert\mathcal I_1\rvert=\lvert\mathcal I_2\rvert=N\)

symbols.name: CB
symbols.def: a deterministic constant computed from \(d,L,\epsilon,\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) and the fixed polynomial bases that bounds the local-polynomial approximation remainder

symbols.name: C0
symbols.def: a deterministic constant computed from \(d,L,\epsilon,\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) and the fixed polynomial bases that bounds the joint coefficient covariance

symbols.name: kn
symbols.def: \(k_n=\dim\mathcal S_{\lceil R_{\mathrm{up}}^{-1/\gamma}\rceil}^{(\lceil\gamma\rceil)}\), the rank of the stated regular-grid signal space

symbols.name: elln
symbols.def: \(\ell_n=\dim\mathcal S_{\lceil R_{\mathrm{up}}^{-1/s}\rceil}^{(\lceil\alpha\vee\beta\rceil)}\), enlarged by the smallest fixed grid level for which \(C_B\ell_n^{-\alpha/d}\le\epsilon(1-\epsilon)/2\)

symbols.name: phiUpper
symbols.def: \(\phi_n^{\mathrm{up}}=0\) for \(n<4\), and \(\phi_n^{\mathrm{up}}=\mathbf 1\{T_{k_n,\ell_n}>t_{k_n,\ell_n}\}\) for \(n\ge4\), with deterministic tie randomization

symbols.name: MixtureHandle
symbols.def: null-preserving full-observation mixture program: perturb the four Bernoulli cell-probability surfaces on a smooth regular partition, enforce constant \(\tau\) in every null draw, moment-match transition regions under exact \(X\sim\lambda\), and optimize the resulting \(\chi^2\) or Hellinger bound subject to the separate \(\mathcal H^\alpha(L)\), \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)\), and \(\mathcal H^\gamma(L)\) constraints
symbols.role: concrete starting move for deriving, rather than guessing, the sharp observational rate

symbols.name: PFullWitness
symbols.def: \(P_t^{\mathrm F,w}\) is generated by \(X\sim\lambda\), \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e^{\mathrm w}(x))\), conditionally independent Bernoulli \(Y(0),Y(1)\) with means \(\mu_0^{\mathrm w}(x)\) and \(\mu_0^{\mathrm w}(x)+\tau_t^{\mathrm w}(x)\), and \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\)

assumptions.condition: Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the covariate law is known and satisfies \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)=\lambda\).
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the potential-outcome vector satisfies \((Y(0),Y(1))\in[0,1]^2\) almost surely.
The full-law propensity satisfies \(e^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L)\).
The full-law propensity satisfies \(\epsilon\le e^{\mathrm F}(x)\le1-\epsilon\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The control potential-outcome regression satisfies \(\mu_0^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)\).
The full-law CATE satisfies \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L)\).
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the observed outcome satisfies \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\) almost surely.

definitions.name: Full-data rough-confounding causal-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon,d)=\{P^{\mathrm F}\in\Delta(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^3):X\sim\lambda,\ (Y(0),Y(1))\in[0,1]^2\ P^{\mathrm F}\text{-a.s.},\ e^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L),\ \epsilon\le e^{\mathrm F}\le1-\epsilon,\ \mu_0^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal H^\beta(L),\ \tau^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L),\ Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\ P^{\mathrm F}\text{-a.s.},\ (Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\}\) over \(\mathcal X=[0,1]^d\), with the conditional joint law of \((Y(0),Y(1))\mid X\) otherwise unrestricted.

definitions.name: Observed-data image of the causal-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon,d)=\{P\in\Delta(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}\times[0,1]):\exists P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon,d),\ P=\operatorname{Obs}(P^{\mathrm F})\}\).

definitions.name: Observed-data minimax separation radius
definitions.construction: \(\rho_\star(n)=\inf\{\rho>0:\exists\text{ measurable }\phi_n:O^n\to[0,1],\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}:\,V(P)=0}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\phi_n(O^n)\le a_0,\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}:\,V(P)\ge\rho^2}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[1-\phi_n(O^n)]\le b_0\}\), with an empty alternative supremum equal to zero.

definitions.name: Known-propensity minimax separation radius
definitions.construction: \(\rho_\star^{\mathrm{known}\ e}(n)=\inf\{\rho>0:\exists\text{ measurable }\phi_n^{\mathrm{known}\ e}:O^n\times\mathcal E_{\alpha,L,\epsilon}\to[0,1],\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}:\,V(P)=0}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\phi_n^{\mathrm{known}\ e}(O^n,e_P)\le a_0,\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}:\,V(P)\ge\rho^2}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[1-\phi_n^{\mathrm{known}\ e}(O^n,e_P)]\le b_0\}\), with the exact propensity \(e_P(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)\) supplied as the second input and an empty alternative supremum equal to zero.

definitions.name: Total corrected-energy test
definitions.construction: Return nonrejection for \(n<4\). For \(n\ge4\), split \(O^n\) into halves of size \(N\); form every coordinate of \(\widehat q_h(c)\) by the displayed order-two U-statistic; compute the three coefficients of the quadratic \(c\mapsto\widehat q_1(c)^\top\widehat q_2(c)\); minimize it on \(I\) by checking both endpoints and the vertex when it is convex and internal; reject exactly when \(T_{k_n,\ell_n}>t_{k_n,\ell_n}\), using \(k_n\) and \(\ell_n\).

definitions.name: Null-preserving observed-data mixture handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathrm{MixtureHandle}\) to the full four-cell Bernoulli likelihood, retaining the transition regions observed under \(X\sim\lambda\); determine the partition scale, moment-matching order, and perturbation amplitudes from the separate Hölder constraints and the requirement that every null draw have constant \(\tau\).

definitions.name: Learner-rate and direction-correlation comparison handle
definitions.construction: Translate Yu (2026), Assumption 4 and Theorem 1 into Hölder sieve rates while retaining \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{Yu},n}(P)\) as a separate applicability restriction. For Dhawan, Guo and Shah (2026), take their predictor to be \(U=(A,X)\), identity-link squared loss, ambient class \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{DGS},P}=L^2(P_U)\), and null class \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{DGS}}\); first derive \(f_P^*\), \(s_P\), and \(\xi_P\) from the two \(L^2\) projections. Compare Corollary 2 only on laws satisfying \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{DGS},n}\), and obtain any claimed strict non-inclusion from an explicit sequence in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\), using dense orthogonal bump packs for vanishing correlation and a single aligned direction for positive correlation.

definitions.name: Nondegenerate polynomial witness
definitions.construction: For \(t\in[0,1/10]\), generate the full law \(P_t^{\mathrm F,w}\) by the declared affine propensity, affine baseline, affine CATE, conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes, and consistency; set \(P_t^{\mathrm w}=\operatorname{Obs}(P_t^{\mathrm F,w})\).

statements.statement: For every \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon,d)\), let \(P=\operatorname{Obs}(P^{\mathrm F})\). Then \(e=e^{\mathrm F}\), \(\mu_a=\mu_a^{\mathrm F}\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and \(\tau=\tau^{\mathrm F}=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X]\), up to \(\lambda\)-null sets. Conversely, every observed law \(P\) with \(X\sim\lambda\), \(Y\in[0,1]\), \(e\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L)\), \(\epsilon\le e\le1-\epsilon\), \(\mu_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)\), and \(\mu_1-\mu_0\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L)\) has a bounded potential-outcome lift in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm F}\), obtained by drawing \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independently from the two observed arm laws given \(X\), drawing \(A\) independently of them given \(X\), and setting \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\). Thus \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is exactly the observed-law class specified by those restrictions.
statements.justification: This bridge makes the causal interpretation and the statistical experiment coexist without placing latent variables inside an observed-law set.
statements.gap: CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 invokes consistency and unconfoundedness for identification; this lemma records the exact observed-image equivalence needed by the minimax experiment.
statements.consumer: Every minimax supremum and likelihood construction can be stated solely over observed laws while retaining an explicit causal estimand.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(c\in I\), \(q_c=w(\tau-c)\). Consequently, \([\epsilon(1-\epsilon)]^2V(P)\le\inf_{c\in I}\|q_c\|_{L^2(\lambda)}^2\le V(P)/16\).
statements.justification: This identity turns homogeneity into a positive profiled conditional-moment energy without inverse propensity weights.
statements.gap: CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 tests constant CATE through a different nonparametric construction and does not state this coercive observed-score reduction.
statements.consumer: The identity supplies the population target for a bounded-weight implementation of the constant-CATE option in the dScoreTest software.

statements.statement: Fix \(P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and specialize Dhawan, Guo and Shah (2026), Section 3.1.1, to predictor \(U=(A,X)\), response \(Y\), identity link, ambient class \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{DGS},P}=L^2(P_U)\), and constant-CATE null class \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{DGS}}\). The null-risk projection is \(f_P^*(A,X)=m(X)+(A-e(X))\bar\tau_w\). Therefore their projected score and debiased hunted direction are, respectively, \(s_P(U)=\mathbb E_P[f_P^*(U)-Y\mid U]=(A-e(X))\{\bar\tau_w-\tau(X)\}\) and \(\xi_P(U)=(A-e(X))\{\widehat h_{\Delta,n}(X)-c_{\widehat h}\}\). It follows that \(V_{\mathrm{DGS}}(P)=\int_{\mathcal X}w(x)\{\tau(x)-\bar\tau_w\}^2\,d\lambda(x)\) and \(\epsilon(1-\epsilon)V(P)\le V_{\mathrm{DGS}}(P)\le V(P)/4\). On a comparison class satisfying \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{DGS},n}\), Corollary 2 therefore applies at \(V(P)\asymp r_n^2\) when its conditional correlation requirement holds and \(n\kappa_n^2r_n^2\to\infty\); the overlap equivalence neither supplies the correlation nor implies the published regularity conditions.
statements.justification: The projection calculation supplies the only faithful bridge from the published direction-correlation theorem to CATE-variance separation.
statements.gap: DhawanGuoShah2026 defines the generic projected score and proves correlation-conditioned power, but does not express the score energy as the overlap-weighted distance from a constant CATE or compare it with a Hölder minimax radius.
statements.consumer: The calculation tells users of \(\texttt{dScoreTest}\) which signal energy its Corollary 2 controls and which alignment and nondegeneracy conditions remain additional.

statements.statement: For the oracle experiment defining \(\rho_\star^{\mathrm{known}\ e}\), whose measurable tests receive \((O^n,e_P)\), \(c_{\mathrm{rate}}r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\le\rho_\star^{\mathrm{known}\ e}(n)\le C_{\mathrm{rate}}r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). The upper bound is attained by a centered projection U-statistic with ranks allowed to exceed \(n\), and the lower bound holds for all such randomized oracle tests by a legal Bernoulli bump mixture in the same observed image with exactly uniform \(X\).
statements.justification: The theorem fixes the nuisance-free benchmark that any claimed observational phase diagram must reproduce.
statements.gap: IngsterSapatinas2009 gives the direct Gaussian-regression benchmark; this theorem must transfer the exponent to the bounded causal Bernoulli experiment with an unknown profiled constant.
statements.consumer: It tells users whether a proposed rough-confounding procedure pays a genuine price beyond a randomized or known-assignment benchmark.

statements.statement: The explicit finite constants \(C_B,C_0,C_{\mathrm{rate}},n_0\) depend only on \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon\) and the fixed polynomial bases, and \(\phi_n^{\mathrm{up}}\) is a terminating measurable test satisfying \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}:\,V(P)=0}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\phi_n^{\mathrm{up}}\le0.05\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}:\,V(P)\ge C_{\mathrm{rate}}^2R_{\mathrm{up}}^2}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}(1-\phi_n^{\mathrm{up}})\le0.20\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). A direct implementation uses \(O((1+n^2)k_n\ell_n^2)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(k_n\ell_n^2+n(k_n+\ell_n))\) storage. Thus \(\rho_\star(n)\le C_{\mathrm{rate}}R_{\mathrm{up}}(n)\).
statements.justification: This is the constructive half: it remains valid when first-order nuisance-product conditions fail and when both sieve ranks exceed sample size.
statements.gap: DhawanGuoShah2026 and Yu2026VarianceHTE require learned-direction or nuisance-rate conditions and do not provide a full Hölder-class separation guarantee with a total test.
statements.consumer: The explicit statistic and conservative critical value provide a calibratable benchmark implementation for \(\texttt{hte\_test\_conditional}\) when regression learners are too rough for first-order theory.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(d\ge1\), \(P_t^{\mathrm F,w}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm F}\), \(P_t^{\mathrm w}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \((P_t^{\mathrm w})^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal M_n\) for each \(t\in[0,1/10]\). This family has \(V(P_t^{\mathrm w})=t^2/12\), strictly positive arm variances, a nonconstant propensity and baseline, and a legal constant-CATE null at \(t=0\).
statements.justification: The proposition rules out vacuity and supplies interior Bernoulli slack for legal likelihood perturbations without imposing an interior-mean restriction on the headline class.
statements.gap: This is a legality check, not the least-favorable mixture or the minimax converse.
statements.consumer: It supplies a regression test fixture for validating any software implementation without pretending to certify its worst-case power.

statements.statement: Derive an explicit rate \(r_n(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\), including every phase boundary and every necessary equality-case logarithm, and prove \(c_{\mathrm{rate}}r_n\le\rho_\star(n)\le C_{\mathrm{rate}}r_n\) over the observed image \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). The upper inequality must be attained by a total data-computable test with uniform size and power; the lower inequality must hold for all randomized tests via priors on observed laws in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) whose full-law null lifts each have constant \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\) and exact uniform design. Determine from the derived formula whether \(r_n=r_{\mathrm{or}}\), and exactly where learning \(e\) and \(\mu_0\) changes the benchmark; \(R_{\mathrm{up}}\) is one candidate upper bound and is not prescribed as the answer.
statements.justification: The same-class converse is the theorem-level kernel; it decides whether rough confounding genuinely alters omnibus detectability rather than merely degrading a particular estimator.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 proves a nuisance elbow for pointwise CATE estimation, while KotekalKundu2025 proves a rough-mean elbow for heteroskedasticity testing; neither supplies constant-CATE testing priors that preserve this model's baseline smoothness and exact uniform design.
statements.consumer: A sharp answer identifies when dScoreTest's first-order hunting route can be omnibus-rate optimal and when a higher-order calibrated alternative is statistically necessary.

statements.statement: Characterize the set of \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\) for which \(\rho_\star(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\), and on its complement derive the exact nuisance-limited exponent with any boundary logarithm. The characterization must distinguish \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) separately whenever two laws with the same sum \(\alpha+\beta\) have different testing difficulty. On each phase, compare minimax-detectable sequences in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with Yu's learner condition \(\mathsf Y_n\) only on laws satisfying \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{Yu},n}(P)\); at \(V(P)\asymp r_n^2\), record separately Yu's root-\(n\) signal requirement \(\sqrt n\,r_n^2\to\infty\). Compare the same sequences with Dhawan--Guo--Shah only on the intersection satisfying \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{DGS},n}\). For DGS, use the DGS score-translation lemma: at \(V(P)\asymp r_n^2\), Corollary 2 additionally requires \(\operatorname{Corr}_P(s_P(U),\xi_P(U)\mid\widehat h_n)>\kappa_n\) with high probability and \(n\kappa_n^2r_n^2\to\infty\). Establish every claimed strict inclusion or non-inclusion by legal sequences in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\), using a dense orthogonal bump pack against the hunted direction and a one-direction aligned alternative as the comparison handle; if either construction fails the full-law lift or a published applicability condition, report that relation as unresolved rather than asserting it. Separate uniform omnibus power from favorable-direction pointwise power.
statements.justification: The phase map must distinguish statistical hardness from the sufficient learner and alignment conditions imposed by currently implementable first-order procedures.
statements.gap: Yu2026VarianceHTE, Assumption 4 and Theorem 1 require separate learner remainders and additional boundary nondegeneracy, while DhawanGuoShah2026, Corollary 2 applies to its projected score on \(U\) under \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{DGS},n}\), conditional correlation above \(\kappa_n\), and \(n\kappa_n^2V_{\mathrm{DGS}}(P)\to\infty\); neither paper locates these sufficient regimes relative to the Hölder minimax radius or proves a class inclusion.
statements.consumer: The resulting verified relation map tells users of the Yu variance test and \(\texttt{dScoreTest}\) when their guarantees reach the omnibus frontier, when favorable alignment yields different pointwise power, and when corrected energy is required.

sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with \(P(A_i=1\mid X_i=x)=e(x)\) and fixed overlap \(\epsilon\le e\le1-\epsilon\).
sampling_model.overlap: The overlap constant \(\epsilon\) is known to the test and does not vary with \(n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No fitted-nuisance rate is assumed; all signal and nuisance grid ranks and every calibration constant are functions only of \(n,d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,\epsilon\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 4.2 defines \(s_P\) as the \(L^2(P_U)\) projection of the loss score onto \(\mathcal G_P\) and \(\xi_P\) as the hunted direction after projection off \(\mathcal F_P\); Corollary 2 gives power over \(\{P:\tau_P\ge\varepsilon_n\}\) when \(\operatorname{Corr}_P(s_P(U),\xi_P(U)\mid\widehat h)>\rho_n\) uniformly with high probability and \(n\rho_n^2\varepsilon_n\to\infty\).

Assumption 4 and Theorem 1 give asymptotic normality for the intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under separate \(o_P(n^{-1/4})\) propensity, outcome-regression, and CATE learner errors and a root-\(n\) ATE error.
Theorem 1 gives the pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate with a nuisance-smoothness elbow.
The main minimax theorems give phasewise heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under rough mean regression.
The paper derives sharp weighted U-tests and minimax constants for regression nulls defined by nonnegative quadratic functionals.
Theorem 1 gives rate-optimal quadratic U-tests for multivariate Gaussian regression under known random uniform design.
Theorem 4 gives a weighted chi-square null limit for a second-order U-statistic testing equality of unknown functions.
The spline specialization gives a minimax projected-covariance test under common smoothness and nondegeneracy conditions.
The paper constructs nonparametric tests for zero and constant conditional average treatment effects under unconfoundedness.

The paper gives an observational treatment-effect heterogeneity test based on propensity-reweighted multisample U-statistics that bypasses modeling the treatment effect in each study subgroup, with an asymptotic normality result.
The paper gives nonparametric quantitative and qualitative homogeneity tests with fixed and local asymptotic power analyses.
The paper gives boundary-robust confidence intervals for explained treatment-effect variance in randomized experiments.

tldr: Constant-CATE testing is posed over the explicit observed-data image of a full causal-law Hölder class, so potential-outcome identification and every minimax supremum now live at the correct levels. A separate oracle radius ranges over measurable tests of \((O^n,e_P)\). A coercive profiled moment and known-design product correction yield an explicit higher-order cross-energy test with candidate upper rate \(R_{\mathrm{up}}=n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\vee n^{-4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)/(4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)+d(\alpha+\beta)+2d\gamma)}\). The central open theorem remains the sharp same-image observational frontier. A risk-projection lemma derives the exact Dhawan--Guo--Shah score on \(U=(A,X)\), showing that its energy is equivalent to \(V(P)\) under overlap while its learner, variance, and direction-correlation restrictions remain additional; the companion phase map compares those restrictions and Yu's learner regime with the uniform minimax radius without claiming subsumption in advance.

project_justification.gap: Existing observational homogeneity tests document asymptotic size and power under learned-direction, learner-remainder, or multisample U-statistic conditions; existing Hölder theory treats CATE estimation, direct regression, conditional-mean independence under different classes, or heteroskedasticity rather than the declared constant-CATE experiment.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the full-class minimax separation radius when the null contains every unknown constant effect and arbitrary permitted rough propensity and baseline functions, including regimes in which both useful sieve ranks exceed sample size and first-order product conditions fail.
project_justification.fill: The project targets an algorithmic upper bound and matching observational converse on one unchanged statistical class through an exact full-law-to-observed-image bridge, a profiled bounded-weight score, deterministic local-polynomial product correction, independent higher-order cross-energy, and a null-preserving observed-likelihood mixture program; the risk-projection lemma places Yu and Dhawan--Guo--Shah on the phase map under their own conditions.

related_work: Dhawan, Guo and Shah (2026), Section 3.1.1, formulate effect-modifier testing as identity-link conditional-mean risk minimization with generic predictor \(U=(A,X)\), an unrestricted-baseline null class, and ambient class \(L^2(P_U)\). Their Section 4.2 defines \(s_P\) as the \(L^2\) projection of the loss score and \(\xi_P\) as the hunted function minus its null-class projection; Corollary 2 requires their regularity and estimation conditions, conditional correlation above \(\rho_n\), and \(n\rho_n^2\varepsilon_n\to\infty\). The score-translation lemma derives, rather than assumes, that the constant-CATE specialization has \(s_P(U)=(A-e(X))(\bar\tau_w-\tau(X))\) and effect energy equivalent to \(V(P)\); it does not infer the required correlation or conditional score-variance bound from the Hölder class. Yu (2026), Assumption 4 and Theorem 1, directly targets CATE variance with intra-fold splitting under separate \(o_P(n^{-1/4})\) learner errors and a root-\(n\) ATE error, while its boundary-nondegeneracy condition is not imposed here. The open phase comparison therefore asks for legal sequences before asserting any non-subsumption. Crump, Hotz, Imbens and Mitnik (2008) provide the classical constant-CATE test. Dai, Shen and Stern (2023), Canadian Journal of Statistics 51(2):531--558, provide a propensity-reweighted multisample U-statistic test for observational treatment-effect heterogeneity that bypasses modeling the treatment effect in each study subgroup; they do not characterize the continuous Hölder minimax frontier. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins and Wasserman (2024) supply the closest causal minimax geometry for pointwise CATE estimation. Kotekal and Kundu (2025), Annals of Statistics 53(1):295--321, give sharp heteroskedasticity-testing rates with a rough mean. Comminges and Dalalyan (2013), Ingster and Sapatinas (2009), Luedtke, Carone and van der Laan (2019), and Lundborg, Kim, Shah and Samworth (2024) inform the quadratic and projected-score constructions under different experiments. Dukes, Stensrud, Brioschi and Hudson (2024) and Sánchez-Becerra (2023) study complementary homogeneity-inference targets rather than this full-class radius.
technical_internal_limitation: The displayed \(R_{\mathrm{up}}\) is an upper-envelope candidate. The presolve's coefficient-covariance bound, simultaneous profiling constants, and numerical basis constants still require complete proof. More importantly, the oracle lower bound proves no nuisance penalty and cannot certify \(R_{\mathrm{up}}\): at \(d=1\), \(\alpha=1/64\), \(\beta=9/64\), and \(\gamma=1/8\), a valid converse must preserve baseline smoothness while accounting for every transition region observed under uniform design. Failure of one mixture construction is not evidence that the nuisance exponent is false.
honest_scope: The target statistical class is exactly the observed image \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) of bounded full causal laws satisfying consistency, conditional exchangeability, exact uniform design, fixed strong overlap, and separate Hölder smoothness for \(e^{\mathrm F}\), \(\mu_0^{\mathrm F}\), and \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\). The observed-image lemma gives the equivalent observed-law restrictions, so minimax tests never receive latent variables. There is no uniform interior arm-mean or conditional-variance lower bound; the affine Bernoulli witness is interior only to provide lower-bound perturbation slack. The DGS comparison is restricted to laws also satisfying that paper's variance, estimation, nondegeneracy, and Lyapunov conditions, and the Yu comparison retains its boundary conditions; neither restriction is added to the minimax class. Unknown design density, smoothness adaptation, and outcomes outside \([0,1]\) are outside scope. The known-propensity benchmark and computable observational upper bound are theorem targets; the matching observational rate, individual smoothness dependence, boundary logarithms, and strict phasewise comparisons remain open. Under supplied propensity, the frontier must reduce to \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\).

seed_details.question: What is the exact minimax \(L^2\) separation radius for an unknown constant CATE under separately rough propensity, baseline, and CATE functions?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the single hunted score direction by a profiled quadratic score energy and replace the first-order nuisance remainder by known-design higher-order product projection.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact searches for constant CATE, Hölder separation, propensity smoothness, CATE variance, and rough confounding found asymptotic homogeneity tests and CATE-estimation minimax results, but no same-class separation theorem.
seed_details.red_team: The boundary is immediate by substituting the Kennedy et al. CATE-estimation rate into a quadratic test.
seed_details.rebuttal: Testing has degenerate quadratic noise and Kennedy et al.'s localized design suppresses transition regions; neither its exponent nor its lower mixture transfers to exact uniform design.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorem 1, localized fuzzy-hypothesis construction in Section 3, higher-order local-polynomial variance argument, and Discussion were opened.
seed_details.question: At which derived smoothness frontier does the observational separation radius cease to equal the known-propensity rate?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pointwise loss by a profiled quadratic testing modulus and force both sides of the fuzzy hypotheses to retain exact uniform design and constant CATE under the null.
seed_details.destination_search: Known-design regression and observational CATE searches found Ingster--Sapatinas and Kennedy et al., but no observed-primitive divergence frontier for these two experiments.
seed_details.red_team: The divergence frontier is just the usual first-order product-rate threshold.
seed_details.rebuttal: The higher-order test remains informative when the first-order product fails, and the unknown-constant degenerate energy has a different stochastic scale; the threshold must be derived from a testing modulus.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The frontier is an output of a matched experiment comparison, not an assumed nuisance penalty.

seed_details.question: Can a treatment-weighted local cross-product proxy improve on corrected direct CATE-energy estimation, or does unrestricted bounded outcome noise make such improvement impossible?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The donor identity \(\mathbb E(R_i^2)=\delta_i^2+W_i\) fails after treatment selection; replace it by cross-products that identify variation while leaving only a product of propensity and baseline projection residuals.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found Luedtke et al. and Yu for direct higher-order CATE functionals, but no sharp proxy-versus-direct dichotomy under bounded unrestricted conditional outcome laws.
seed_details.red_team: Kotekal--Kundu's first-difference proof transfers after inverse-propensity weighting.
seed_details.rebuttal: Treatment weighting introduces an unknown propensity and their roughest improvements use Gaussian noise information absent from the bounded-outcome model.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed requires either a matched proxy frontier or a full-class impossibility theorem, not a sufficient statistic alone.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Section 3.1.1, Section 4.1, Section 4.2 equations (15)--(17), Theorem 1, Corollaries 1--2, and Lemmas S10--S11 were opened; the paper defines the risk classes, the projected score on its generic predictor, and correlation-conditioned power.
seed_details.question: Can one uniformly valid test attain the directional boundary on aligned alternatives and the quadratic boundary on dense Hölder alternatives over their union?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Couple an independently hunted linear score with a corrected projected energy and calibrate their joint maximum under shared nuisance fits.
seed_details.destination_search: PCM covers a learned projection and Comminges--Dalalyan covers dense quadratic alternatives, but no rough-confounding hybrid with two matched class-specific lower bounds was located.
seed_details.red_team: A Bonferroni union of the two published tests immediately adapts.
seed_details.rebuttal: Neither component has a full Hölder boundary on this class, and shared rough nuisances alter both calibration and the adaptation lower bound.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed promises two class-specific minimax boundaries, not merely a combined p-value.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The wavelet multiscale construction, adaptive upper theorem, lower mixture establishing an unavoidable iterated-logarithm loss, Introduction, and concluding discussion were opened through the journal and WIAS records.
seed_details.question: What is the exact adaptation penalty when one constant-CATE test does not know \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) and crosses nuisance-driven phase boundaries?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Gaussian wavelet coefficients by simultaneously calibrated corrected CATE energies indexed by target and nuisance resolutions.
seed_details.destination_search: Fromont--Laurent gives multiple quadratic-distance calibration and Spokoiny gives the classical lower cost, but no causal multiscale result adapts across a nuisance elbow.
seed_details.red_team: The ordinary \(\log\log n\) factor follows directly from Spokoiny's multiscale test.
seed_details.rebuttal: An unknown nuisance phase adds a second resolution and a composite constant null; whether it adds a separate penalty is precisely not covered by classical signal detection.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Deferred until the fixed-smoothness rate is known, since otherwise the oracle comparator is undefined.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The composite quadratic-functional null, optimized linear U-test, extremal weighting theorem, lower-prior proof, Introduction, and conclusion were opened.
seed_details.question: What is the sharp separation rate from a known \(q_n\)-dimensional CATE space when \(q_n\) grows and rough confounding must be corrected?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project the nuisance-corrected CATE score off the null space before forming cross-energy, then quantify the interaction between profiling rank and nuisance resolution.
seed_details.destination_search: Dhawan et al. test linear regression classes directionally; no omnibus causal rate with growing null dimension was located.
seed_details.red_team: This is the constant-null proof with one projection matrix inserted.
seed_details.rebuttal: Growing \(q_n\) changes degeneracy, profiling noise, and least-favorable directions, so the \(q_n\)-phase cannot be inferred from the one-dimensional null.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Not selected because the \(q_n=1\) same-class converse must be solved first.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction and CATE example, Theorem 2 second-order pathwise derivative, Theorem 4 weighted chi-square null limit and proof, local-alternative theorem, and discussion were opened.
seed_details.question: What is the phasewise null and local-alternative limit law of the corrected CATE energy as effective projection rank moves from fixed to divergent through nuisance-limited regimes?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a fixed Hilbert--Schmidt kernel spectrum by a two-resolution triangular kernel with deterministic product drift and ranks potentially above \(n\).
seed_details.destination_search: Yu obtains an ordinary Gaussian studentization by intra-fold splitting and Luedtke et al. obtain a fixed-kernel weighted chi-square law; no mixed triangular-array law through rough-confounding phases was found.
seed_details.red_team: Classical degenerate U-statistic theory already supplies the limit.
seed_details.rebuttal: The kernel, rank, product drift, and nuisance correction all change with \(n\); fixed-spectrum theory does not provide uniform calibration across the transition.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a limit-law kernel rather than a disguised matched-rate seed.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Proposition on non-orthogonal splitting bias, Algorithm 1, Theorem 1 and its proof, Appendix B naive-statistic expansion, and Conclusion were opened.
seed_details.question: Can a second-order local asymptotic experiment at the constant-CATE boundary characterize an information envelope and an attaining quadratic test under rough confounding?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the regular first-order tangent calculation, whose derivative vanishes at homogeneity, by a Hölder-constrained second-order tangent cone with nuisance profiling.
seed_details.destination_search: Luedtke et al. derive a second-order canonical gradient and Sánchez-Becerra handles boundary inference in experiments, but no rough observational Hölder information envelope was located.
seed_details.red_team: Semiparametric efficiency is zero or undefined at a quadratic boundary, so the question is ill posed.
seed_details.rebuttal: The ordinary first-order bound is degenerate, but a specified second-order local experiment can have a nontrivial power envelope; the object must be formulated on the tangent cone rather than called a regular efficiency bound.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Retained as a credible nonregular information problem but not selected because it may not yield the global minimax frontier.

seed_details.question: Can a finite-sample symmetry orbit test constant CATE after observational propensity adjustment?

novelty_justification: The closest causal comparator is DhawanGuoShah2026, whose Corollary 2 gives first-order power under its own regularity conditions when a direction on the full predictor \(U\) correlates with the \(L^2(P_U)\)-projected loss score. The score-translation lemma derives that projection for the declared constant-CATE problem and isolates the remaining alignment and variance restrictions. The closest causal minimax comparator is KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024, whose target is pointwise CATE estimation, and the closest rough-nuisance testing comparator is KotekalKundu2025, whose experiment is heteroskedasticity testing. The strict unoccupied object is the full-observation constant-CATE testing modulus over the exact observed image of the declared causal Hölder class. Its upper-bound step is a known-design augmented product correction; its converse must preserve a constant full-law CATE and exact uniform design in every null draw. The companion phase map compares this uniform modulus with Yu's learner conditions and DGS's correlation-conditioned power only on their actual applicability classes, with strict relations contingent on explicit legal witnesses.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: The minimax bracket and exact no-penalty phase for testing treatment-effect heterogeneity with rough confounding. For fixed d>=1, alpha,beta,gamma>0, Holder radius L>=2, and overlap epsilon in (0,1/4), observe n iid O=(X,A,Y), with X uniform on [0,1]^d, A binary, Y in [0,1], propensity e in H^alpha(L) satisfying epsilon<=e<=1-epsilon, baseline mu0=E[Y|A=0,X] in H^beta(L), and CATE tau=mu1-mu0 in H^gamma(L). Consistency and conditional exchangeability identify tau; the experiment is the observed-data image of the corresponding full causal-law class. No interior arm-mean restriction, conditional-variance floor, or fitted-nuisance rate is assumed. Let V(P)=integral (tau-integral tau)^2 and rho_star(n) be the constant-CATE minimax separation radius at size 0.05 and type-II error 0.20 over this same observed-law class. Prove the full-class two-sided bracket c*r_or(n)<=rho_star(n)<=C*max(r_or(n),r_nu(n)), with explicit powers r_or=n^(-2gamma/(4gamma+d)) and r_nu=n^(-4gamma(alpha+beta)/(4gamma(alpha+beta)+d(alpha+beta)+2dgamma)). Prove the exact no-penalty phase rho_star(n) asymptotic to r_or(n) when alpha+beta>=2dgamma/(4gamma+d), including equality without logarithmic loss. Supply an explicitly computable, terminating, uniformly calibrated higher-order corrected-energy test attaining the upper endpoint, with deterministic tuning from the declared class constants and stated arithmetic complexity. Treat only the complementary rough regime alpha+beta<2dgamma/(4gamma+d) as open: whether r_nu is sharp, whether alpha and beta enter separately through further elbows, and whether logarithms occur there. Compare this continuous-design CATE-variance testing problem locally with the discrete arbitrary-cell-mass scalar-ATE bracket stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier/v1 and with the additional learner/direction/variance conditions of Yu (2026) and Dhawan--Guo--Shah (2026), without claiming those procedures give a uniform full-class minimax converse.
